judgment.notes: S001's equal pieces cover [0,1], and for each fixed scale and tolerance one sufficiently large N makes both mesh and a-cost small (BG001–BG006). S002's finite diameters bound each nonempty W_i, so its explicitly enlarged endpoints give covering open intervals of the asserted lengths (BG007–BG008). S003 uses countable subadditivity only after enlargement, obtains ∑ρ_i≥1 without assuming summability, and uses the correctly reversed negative-exponent inequality; zero diameters and infinite sums are handled (BG009–BG013, BG016–BG017). S004's power bound is unbounded as δ↓0 with s fixed (BG014), giving infinite measure and the lower dimension bound, not an unjustified limit exchange. S005 pulls every F-cover back along a genuine isometric vertical copy, compares positive powers (BG015), then takes infima and suprema in the correct directions. Dimension bounds for every 0<v<1 imply ≥1 also if dimension is infinite. The argument includes n=0 and the D=0 implication.

The conditional premises are exactly H001, M004, M005, M006 and E001. H001 supplies x0∈E; the three M statements are used for Lebesgue measure on ℝ and countable interval families, and E001 is instantiated only at positive exponents on the specified Euclidean sets. No input N or producer body is assumed. Source authenticity is outside this conditional review.
